sentences.text: Blasisaurus was a medium-sized ornithopod, a type of herbivorous dinosaur known for their beaked jaws.

The type species Blasisaurus canudoi was described in 2010 by Spanish researchers who studied disarticulated cranial remains found since 1997 in the upper part of the Arén Formation in Huesca province, Spain.
The specific epithet honors paleontologist José Ignacio Canudo, and the holotype specimen, MPZ99/667, is currently housed in Huesca.
Additional remains of Blasisaurus sp. were later found and described at the Les Serretes paleontological site in Vilamitjana.
Blasisaurus belongs to the subfamily Lambeosaurinae, a group of duck-billed dinosaurs characterized by hollow cranial crests.
Phylogenetic analysis placed Blasisaurus as the sister taxon to Arenysaurus, together forming a clade that is more derived in Lambeosaurinae than Tsintaosaurus and Jaxartosaurus.

It lived at the end of the Cretaceous period, approximately 66 million years ago, during the upper Maastrichtian in what is now Europe. The time range for Blasisaurus is the Maastrichtian, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
The placement of Blasisaurus and Arenysaurus within Lambeosaurinae is debated, with some studies placing them in Lambeosaurini and others in Parasaurolophini.
